stem: At a fabric shop in Faisalabad, cotton costs 400 rupees per meter and silk costs 1,100 rupees per meter. A customer bought 14 meters of fabric in all, and she paid 3,400 rupees more for the silk than for the cotton. How many meters of cotton did she buy?
solution: Let \(c\) be the meters of cotton and \(s\) the meters of silk: \(c + s = 14\) and \(1{,}100s - 400c = 3{,}400\).
Then \(1{,}500c = 12{,}000\) and \(c = 8\). (Check: 6 meters of silk cost 6,600 rupees and 8 meters of cotton cost 3,200 rupees.)
verify:
c, s = symbols('c s')
sol = solve([c + s - 14, 1100*s - 400*c - 3400], [c, s])
assert sol == {c: 8, s: 6}
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [sol[c]]
